**Best Buy Co., Inc.** is an American multinational consumer electronics retailer headquartered in Richfield, Minnesota. Originally founded by Richard M. Schulze and James Wheeler in 1966 as an audio specialty store called Sound of Music, it was rebranded under its current name with an emphasis on consumer electronics in 1983.
Best Buy operates internationally in Canada, and formerly operated in China until February 2011 (when the faction was merged with Five Star) and in Mexico until December 2020 (due to the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic). The company also operated in Europe until 2012. Its subsidiaries include Geek Squad, Magnolia Audio Video, and Pacific Sales. Best Buy also operates the Best Buy Mobile and Insignia brands in North America, plus Five Star in China.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-SEC-4) Best Buy sells cellular phones from Verizon Wireless, AT&T Mobility, T-Mobile, Boost Mobile and Ting Mobile[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-5) in the United States. In Canada, carriers include Bell Mobility, Rogers Wireless, Telus Mobility, their fighter brands, and competing smaller carriers, such as SaskTel.
According to Yahoo! Finance, Best Buy is the largest specialty retailer in the United States consumer electronics retail industry.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-6) The company ranked number 72 in the 2018 _Fortune_ 500 list of the largest United States corporations by total revenue.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-7)

## History
### Early history
Sound of Music logo used from 1980 until 1984
On August 22, 1966, Richard M. Schulze and a business partner opened Sound of Music, an electronics store specializing in high fidelity stereos in St. Paul, Minnesota.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15) Schulze financed the opening of his first store with his personal savings and a second mortgage he took out on his family's home.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16) In 1967, Sound of Music acquired Kencraft Hi-Fi Company and Bergo Company.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16) Sound of Music earned $1 million in revenue and made about $58,000 in profits in its first year.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14) In 1969, Sound of Music had three stores[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-17) and Schulze bought out his business partner.

## History
### Early history
Sound of Music operated nine stores throughout Minnesota by 1978.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneyears-18) In 1981, the Roseville location, at the time the largest and most profitable Sound of Music store, was hit by a tornado.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14) The store's roof was sheared off and showroom destroyed, but the storeroom was left intact.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) In response, Schulze decided to have a "Tornado Sale" of damaged and excess stock in the damaged store's parking lot.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14) He poured the remainder of his marketing budget into advertising the sale, promising "best buys" on everything.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) Sound of Music made more money during the four-day sale than it did in a typical month.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15)
Best Buy Co. logo from 1984 until 1986 (but the "Superstores" variant, added in March 1986)
Best Buy Superstores logo from 1986 until 1989

## History
### Early history
In 1983, with seven stores and $10 million in annual sales, Sound of Music was renamed Best Buy Company, Inc.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneyears-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) The company also expanded its product offerings to include home appliances and VCRs, in an attempt to expand beyond its then-core customer base of 15- to 18-year-old males. Later that year, Best Buy opened its first superstore in Burnsville, Minnesota.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) The Burnsville location featured a high-volume, low-price business model, which was borrowed partially from Schulze's successful Tornado Sale in 1981.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) In its first year, the Burnsville store out-performed all other Best Buy stores combined.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16)
Best Buy was taken public in 1985, and two years later it debuted on the New York Stock Exchange.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21) In 1988, Best Buy was in a price and location war with Detroit-based appliance chain Highland Superstores, and Schulze attempted to sell the company to Circuit City for US$30 million. Circuit City rejected the offer, claiming they could open a store in Minneapolis and "blow them away."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-22)

## History
### Early history
In 1988, the company introduced a new store concept dubbed "Concept II".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20) Concept II replaced dimly lit industrial-style stores with brighter and more fashionably fixtured stores.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16) Stores also began placing all stock on the sales floor rather than in a stock room, had fewer salespersons and provided more self-help product information for its customers.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21) Best Buy also did away with commissioned salespeople.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20) The commission-free sales environment "created a more relaxed shopping environment free of the high-pressure sales tactics used in other stores," but was unpopular with salespersons and suppliers.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20) Upset that their products would no longer be pushed by salespeople, some suppliers such as Maytag, Whirlpool, and Sony stopped selling in Best Buy stores altogether.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15) The suppliers returned after Best Buy's sales and revenue grew following the roll-out of Concept II.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19)
In 1992, the company achieved $1 billion in annual revenues.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21) Its Midwest rival, Highland, would file for bankruptcy in the same year and close all locations by 1993.

## History
### Early history
In 1994, Best Buy debuted "Concept III" stores in several new markets including Los Angeles and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenews11-23) Concept III stores were larger than previous stores and included expanded product offerings, "Answer Center" touchscreen kiosks that displayed product information for both customers and employees, and demonstration areas for products such as surround sound stereo systems and video games.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenews11-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-customerelectronics-24)
Best Buy launched its "Concept IV" stores with its expansion into New England in 1998.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenews26-25) Concept IV stores included an open layout with products organized by category, cash registers located throughout the store, and slightly smaller stores than Concept III stores.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunemoore-26) The stores also had large areas for demonstrating home theater systems and computer software.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-providencenew-27)
In 1999, Best Buy was added to [Standard & Poor's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_&_Poor's "Standard & Poor's")S&P 500.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)

## History
### 2000s
In 2000, Best Buy formed Redline Entertainment, an independent music label and action-sports video distributor.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-newswire-28) The company acquired Magnolia Hi-Fi, Inc., an audio-video retailer located in California, Washington, and Oregon, in December 2000.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)
In January 2001, Best Buy acquired Musicland Stores Corporation, a Minnetonka, Minnesota-based retailer that sold home-entertainment products under the Sam Goody, Suncoast Motion Picture Company, Media Play, and OnCue brands. Best Buy purchased the company for $425 million in cash and the assumption of $271 million of Musicland debt.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-audioweek-29) Later that year, Best Buy acquired the British Columbia, Canada-based electronics-chain Future Shop Ltd., marking its entrance to the international marketplace.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenewscn-30) Under the deal, Future Shop was purchased for about US$377 million and continued to operate as subsidiary independent from Best Buy Canada.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-saint-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-32)

## History
### 2000s
Brad Anderson succeeded Richard Schulze as Best Buy CEO in July 2002.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunegeek-33) Anderson began working at Best Buy in 1973 while attending seminary school.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunegeek-33) He was promoted to vice president in 1981 and executive vice president in 1986. Anderson had most recently been president and COO of Best Buy, a position he had held since 1991.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunegeek-33) In September of that year, Best Buy opened the first Canadian Best Buy-branded store in Mississauga, Ontario.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenewson-34) In October, Best Buy acquired Minneapolis-based Geek Squad, then a 24-hour residential computer repair business with offices in Minneapolis, Chicago, Los Angeles, and San Francisco.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunegeek-33)
Best Buy stores in the U.S. surpassed the 600-store mark and the company opened its first global-sourcing office in Shanghai in 2003.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-billboard600-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-shanghaidaily-36) In June, Best Buy divested Musicland to Sun Capital Partners in exchange for all its stock and debt.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-mergersacquis-37) Best Buy launched its "Reward Zone" loyalty program in July following an 8-month test of the program in San Diego, California.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-warrens-38) Also in 2003, Best Buy's corporate offices were consolidated into a single campus in Richfield, Minnesota.

## History
### 2000s
In January 2004, Best Buy hired Virtucom Group to revamp Best Buy's website and handle all of the company's online content.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-virtucom-39) In May, the company launched its "customer centricity" program, which segmented its stores according to customer profiles. The program also called for employees to focus on specific customer groups rather than product categories.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-40) In October, Best Buy completed rolling out Geek Squad "precincts" in every American Best Buy store.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-financialtimes-41)
In April 2005, Best Buy began eliminating mail-in rebates in response to negative customer reaction against them, and instead started giving out instant rebates via notebook computers.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-twincityjournal-42)
In May 2006, Best Buy acquired a majority interest in Chinese appliance retailer Jiangsu Five Star Appliance for $180 million. At the time of the deal, Jiangsu was the fourth-largest appliance chain in China with 193 stores across eight Chinese provinces.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-xinhua-43) In June, the company opened Geek Squad precincts at Office Depot in Orlando, Florida.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-warrens-38) The market test was later expanded to Denver.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-odearnings-44)

## Controversies
### Analog televisions
On April 26, 2008, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) fined the company $280,000 for not alerting customers that the analog televisions it sold would not receive over-the-air stations after the digital transition on June 12, 2009.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-101) The company challenged this ruling in May 2008 by the FCC saying it was and is in compliance with current FCC regulations pertaining to the digital transition.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-102)

## Controversies
### Environmental issues
Best Buy was one of several companies named in a 2007 report by Greenpeace for purchasing raw materials or manufactured products derived thereof from logging companies that, in the opinion of Greenpeace, contribute to unethical deforestation of taiga in Canada.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-103)
Since that time, however, the company launched what it calls Greener Together to increase the energy efficiency of its products, and reduce consumer waste through more recyclable packaging and proper disposal of certain electronic components such as rechargeable batteries and empty ink cartridges.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-104)
As a way to improve its image and past environmental issues, the company introduced a recycling program in 2009 that has since collected nearly half-a-billion pounds of consumer electronics and e-waste, and is available at all their stores for a nominal fee. These items are then handed over to certified recyclers in the U.S. for proper recycling. The company's goal is to collect one billion pounds of recycling.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-105)
It also has been named to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency top-50 list of the largest green-power purchasers. In 2011, the company purchased nearly 119 million kilowatt-hours of green power– electricity generated from renewable resources, such as wind, solar, geothermal, biogas, biomass, and low-impact hydropower.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-106)

## Controversies
### FBI collaboration
In their attempt to combat child pornography, the FBI hired several Best Buy employees from the Geek Squad division to covertly work for them flagging potential targets. In one incident, a customer brought in his computer for troubleshooting, which a Best Buy employee flagged as containing images of child pornography and reported to the FBI. The customer was indicted for possession of child pornography, although the judge in the case later threw out nearly all the evidence against the defendant due to "false and misleading statements" made by an FBI agent while trying to secure a search warrant for the customer's house, and the government ultimately dropped the case.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-107)

## Controversies
### Privacy
On October 20, 2023, CBC News released the results of a _Marketplace_ investigation which found that Best Buy technicians had viewed private files, such as intimate photos, on customer devices. One technician was also caught copying photos onto a USB flash drive.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-108)

## Controversies
### LGBT issues
In March 2024, following threats of shareholder-related action from conservative advocacy groups, Best Buy agreed to block donations by employee resource groups to eight LGBT organizations, over their support for access to gender affirming care for trans minors. This was met with criticism by a number of groups, including GLAAD and the Human Rights Campaign.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-109)

## Controversies
### Disability discrimination
In April 2021, Best Buy fired a Coquitlam, British Columbia worker due to a knee injury. Best Buy knew that the worker wanted to keep working; they first started working for Best Buy in Coquitlam in 2018.
In February 2021, he told The B.C. Human Rights Tribunal, about knee pain he had a few months before. After talks with doctors he was told to only stand for 15 minutes. He tried to get accommodations with the store, and he also applied for jobs within the store.
He was fired on April 28, 2021.
In August of 2026, the tribunal told Best Buy to pay him $38,750 for the lost wages, $1,589 for compensation, and $20,000 in compensation for the injury.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-110)

In Canada, carriers include Bell Mobility, Rogers Wireless, Telus Mobility, their fighter brands, and competing smaller carriers, such as SaskTel.
According to Yahoo! Finance, Best Buy is the largest specialty retailer in the United States consumer electronics retail industry.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-6) The company ranked number 72 in the 2018 _Fortune_ 500 list of the largest United States corporations by total revenue.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-7)
texts.2:
## History
### Early history
Sound of Music logo used from 1980 until 1984
On August 22, 1966, Richard M. Schulze and a business partner opened Sound of Music, an electronics store specializing in high fidelity stereos in St. Paul, Minnesota.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15) Schulze financed the opening of his first store with his personal savings and a second mortgage he took out on his family's home.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16) In 1967, Sound of Music acquired Kencraft Hi-Fi Company and Bergo Company.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16) Sound of Music earned $1 million in revenue and made about $58,000 in profits in its first year.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14) In 1969, Sound of Music had three stores[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-17) and Schulze bought out his business partner.
texts.3:
## History
### Early history
Sound of Music operated nine stores throughout Minnesota by 1978.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneyears-18) In 1981, the Roseville location, at the time the largest and most profitable Sound of Music store, was hit by a tornado.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14) The store's roof was sheared off and showroom destroyed, but the storeroom was left intact.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) In response, Schulze decided to have a "Tornado Sale" of damaged and excess stock in the damaged store's parking lot.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14) He poured the remainder of his marketing budget into advertising the sale, promising "best buys" on everything.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) Sound of Music made more money during the four-day sale than it did in a typical month.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15)
Best Buy Co. logo from 1984 until 1986 (but the "Superstores" variant, added in March 1986)
Best Buy Superstores logo from 1986 until 1989
texts.4:
## History
### Early history
In 1983, with seven stores and $10 million in annual sales, Sound of Music was renamed Best Buy Company, Inc.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneyears-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) The company also expanded its product offerings to include home appliances and VCRs, in an attempt to expand beyond its then-core customer base of 15- to 18-year-old males. Later that year, Best Buy opened its first superstore in Burnsville, Minnesota.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) The Burnsville location featured a high-volume, low-price business model, which was borrowed partially from Schulze's successful Tornado Sale in 1981.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) In its first year, the Burnsville store out-performed all other Best Buy stores combined.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16)
Best Buy was taken public in 1985, and two years later it debuted on the New York Stock Exchange.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21) In 1988, Best Buy was in a price and location war with Detroit-based appliance chain Highland Superstores, and Schulze attempted to sell the company to Circuit City for US$30 million. Circuit City rejected the offer, claiming they could open a store in Minneapolis and "blow them away."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-22)
texts.5:
## History
### Early history
In 1988, the company introduced a new store concept dubbed "Concept II".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20) Concept II replaced dimly lit industrial-style stores with brighter and more fashionably fixtured stores.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16) Stores also began placing all stock on the sales floor rather than in a stock room, had fewer salespersons and provided more self-help product information for its customers.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21) Best Buy also did away with commissioned salespeople.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20) The commission-free sales environment "created a more relaxed shopping environment free of the high-pressure sales tactics used in other stores," but was unpopular with salespersons and suppliers.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20) Upset that their products would no longer be pushed by salespeople, some suppliers such as Maytag, Whirlpool, and Sony stopped selling in Best Buy stores altogether.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15) The suppliers returned after Best Buy's sales and revenue grew following the roll-out of Concept II.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19)
In 1992, the company achieved $1 billion in annual revenues.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21) Its Midwest rival, Highland, would file for bankruptcy in the same year and close all locations by 1993.
texts.6:
## History
### Early history
In 1994, Best Buy debuted "Concept III" stores in several new markets including Los Angeles and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenews11-23) Concept III stores were larger than previous stores and included expanded product offerings, "Answer Center" touchscreen kiosks that displayed product information for both customers and employees, and demonstration areas for products such as surround sound stereo systems and video games.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenews11-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-customerelectronics-24)
Best Buy launched its "Concept IV" stores with its expansion into New England in 1998.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenews26-25) Concept IV stores included an open layout with products organized by category, cash registers located throughout the store, and slightly smaller stores than Concept III stores.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunemoore-26) The stores also had large areas for demonstrating home theater systems and computer software.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-providencenew-27)
In 1999, Best Buy was added to [Standard & Poor's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_&_Poor's "Standard & Poor's")S&P 500.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)
texts.7:
## History
### 2000s
In 2000, Best Buy formed Redline Entertainment, an independent music label and action-sports video distributor.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-newswire-28) The company acquired Magnolia Hi-Fi, Inc., an audio-video retailer located in California, Washington, and Oregon, in December 2000.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)
In January 2001, Best Buy acquired Musicland Stores Corporation, a Minnetonka, Minnesota-based retailer that sold home-entertainment products under the Sam Goody, Suncoast Motion Picture Company, Media Play, and OnCue brands. Best Buy purchased the company for $425 million in cash and the assumption of $271 million of Musicland debt.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-audioweek-29) Later that year, Best Buy acquired the British Columbia, Canada-based electronics-chain Future Shop Ltd., marking its entrance to the international marketplace.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenewscn-30) Under the deal, Future Shop was purchased for about US$377 million and continued to operate as subsidiary independent from Best Buy Canada.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-saint-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-32)
texts.8:
## History
### 2000s
Brad Anderson succeeded Richard Schulze as Best Buy CEO in July 2002.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunegeek-33) Anderson began working at Best Buy in 1973 while attending seminary school.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunegeek-33) He was promoted to vice president in 1981 and executive vice president in 1986. Anderson had most recently been president and COO of Best Buy, a position he had held since 1991.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunegeek-33) In September of that year, Best Buy opened the first Canadian Best Buy-branded store in Mississauga, Ontario.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenewson-34) In October, Best Buy acquired Minneapolis-based Geek Squad, then a 24-hour residential computer repair business with offices in Minneapolis, Chicago, Los Angeles, and San Francisco.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunegeek-33)
Best Buy stores in the U.S. surpassed the 600-store mark and the company opened its first global-sourcing office in Shanghai in 2003.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-billboard600-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-shanghaidaily-36) In June, Best Buy divested Musicland to Sun Capital Partners in exchange for all its stock and debt.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-mergersacquis-37) Best Buy launched its "Reward Zone" loyalty program in July following an 8-month test of the program in San Diego, California.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-warrens-38) Also in 2003, Best Buy's corporate offices were consolidated into a single campus in Richfield, Minnesota.
texts.9:
## History
### 2000s
In January 2004, Best Buy hired Virtucom Group to revamp Best Buy's website and handle all of the company's online content.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-virtucom-39) In May, the company launched its "customer centricity" program, which segmented its stores according to customer profiles. The program also called for employees to focus on specific customer groups rather than product categories.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-40) In October, Best Buy completed rolling out Geek Squad "precincts" in every American Best Buy store.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-financialtimes-41)
In April 2005, Best Buy began eliminating mail-in rebates in response to negative customer reaction against them, and instead started giving out instant rebates via notebook computers.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-twincityjournal-42)
In May 2006, Best Buy acquired a majority interest in Chinese appliance retailer Jiangsu Five Star Appliance for $180 million. At the time of the deal, Jiangsu was the fourth-largest appliance chain in China with 193 stores across eight Chinese provinces.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-xinhua-43) In June, the company opened Geek Squad precincts at Office Depot in Orlando, Florida.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-warrens-38) The market test was later expanded to Denver.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-odearnings-44)
texts.28:
## Controversies
### Analog televisions
On April 26, 2008, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) fined the company $280,000 for not alerting customers that the analog televisions it sold would not receive over-the-air stations after the digital transition on June 12, 2009.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-101) The company challenged this ruling in May 2008 by the FCC saying it was and is in compliance with current FCC regulations pertaining to the digital transition.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-102)
texts.29:
## Controversies
### Environmental issues
Best Buy was one of several companies named in a 2007 report by Greenpeace for purchasing raw materials or manufactured products derived thereof from logging companies that, in the opinion of Greenpeace, contribute to unethical deforestation of taiga in Canada.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-103)
Since that time, however, the company launched what it calls Greener Together to increase the energy efficiency of its products, and reduce consumer waste through more recyclable packaging and proper disposal of certain electronic components such as rechargeable batteries and empty ink cartridges.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-104)
As a way to improve its image and past environmental issues, the company introduced a recycling program in 2009 that has since collected nearly half-a-billion pounds of consumer electronics and e-waste, and is available at all their stores for a nominal fee. These items are then handed over to certified recyclers in the U.S. for proper recycling. The company's goal is to collect one billion pounds of recycling.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-105)
It also has been named to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency top-50 list of the largest green-power purchasers. In 2011, the company purchased nearly 119 million kilowatt-hours of green power– electricity generated from renewable resources, such as wind, solar, geothermal, biogas, biomass, and low-impact hydropower.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-106)
texts.30:
## Controversies
### FBI collaboration
In their attempt to combat child pornography, the FBI hired several Best Buy employees from the Geek Squad division to covertly work for them flagging potential targets. In one incident, a customer brought in his computer for troubleshooting, which a Best Buy employee flagged as containing images of child pornography and reported to the FBI. The customer was indicted for possession of child pornography, although the judge in the case later threw out nearly all the evidence against the defendant due to "false and misleading statements" made by an FBI agent while trying to secure a search warrant for the customer's house, and the government ultimately dropped the case.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-107)
texts.31:
## Controversies
### Privacy
On October 20, 2023, CBC News released the results of a _Marketplace_ investigation which found that Best Buy technicians had viewed private files, such as intimate photos, on customer devices. One technician was also caught copying photos onto a USB flash drive.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-108)
texts.32:
## Controversies
### LGBT issues
In March 2024, following threats of shareholder-related action from conservative advocacy groups, Best Buy agreed to block donations by employee resource groups to eight LGBT organizations, over their support for access to gender affirming care for trans minors. This was met with criticism by a number of groups, including GLAAD and the Human Rights Campaign.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-109)
texts.33:
## Controversies
### Disability discrimination
In April 2021, Best Buy fired a Coquitlam, British Columbia worker due to a knee injury. Best Buy knew that the worker wanted to keep working; they first started working for Best Buy in Coquitlam in 2018.
In February 2021, he told The B.C. Human Rights Tribunal, about knee pain he had a few months before. After talks with doctors he was told to only stand for 15 minutes. He tried to get accommodations with the store, and he also applied for jobs within the store.
He was fired on April 28, 2021.
In August of 2026, the tribunal told Best Buy to pay him $38,750 for the lost wages, $1,589 for compensation, and $20,000 in compensation for the injury.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-110)
